author: Hodgson, 1845

art.subject: White-tailed Robin (Myiomela leucura), adult male, a vagrant in shaded Korean island forest: almost entirely blackish-blue, darkest on the face and underparts; forehead and brow shining cobalt-blue, and a glossy blue patch at the shoulder; a white patch near the base of the outer tail feathers on each side, flashed when the tail is spread; a small white patch on the side of the neck usually hidden. Bill black; eye dark; legs blackish.
art.pose: standing on a mossy rock in the forest understorey with the tail half fanned, side view
art.scene: dark evergreen ravine forest with ferns and mossy rocks on a southern Korean island in spring (April), subdued light; no people, buildings or text
art.build: A medium-sized, long-tailed forest chat, clearly larger than a sparrow, slim and upright on fairly long legs; often fans and flicks its tail and droops its wings. Bill black, slender, shorter than the head. Legs long and blackish. Wings short and rounded; the wingtips reach only a little past the tail base. Tail long and square-ended, blackish-blue, the white patches near the base of the outer feathers mostly visible when the tail fans.
avoid: Do not paint a white tail tip or wholly white outer tail feathers; the white is a patch near the base of the outer feathers.
Do not paint an orange or white belly (niltavas, bluethroats); the male's underparts are blackish-blue.
Do not show the hidden white neck patch as a large obvious collar.
Do not make the bird bright sky-blue overall; it looks almost black in shade, with only the forehead and shoulder glossed blue.
